gen-dafont-azonix-gf-lisu-bosa: Ruler-straight strokes give Azonix its stern look. Lisu Bosa, a text serif, adds tall, sturdy lowercase and a lightly flexed contrast that softens the rigid lines above it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-marcellus-sc: Gentle tapering, like a sharpened pencil line, runs through Marcellus SC. Against Azonix, which has no thick-thin shift at all, that small swell becomes the pair's strongest quality: stiff wire above, literary warmth below.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-montagu-slab: Azonix stamps out wide letters whose diagonals match its stems. Montagu Slab, a classic serif with a sizable x-height, can sit at a generous size, letting its moderate swelling carry the text.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-serif-hentaiga: Small letters stand nearly as tall as capitals in Noto Serif Hentaigana, with open curves. Azonix traces every glyph at one thickness, while the body's quiet shift in weight, like brushed watercolor, is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-ovo: Ovo keeps its middle band tall and its ascenders shallow. Azonix, bent from a single length of wire, makes a stiff partner for the moderate thick-thin transitions of this text serif.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-esteban: Precise and modern up top, Blockletter draws unshaded, constant strokes with a squat brush-pen belly. Esteban, a text serif with oversized lowercase, reads smoothly, its stems a touch heavier than the crossbars.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-faustina: Stroke ends as wide as the middle make Blockletter look sketched with a pencil that never presses harder. Faustina's soft fat-to-slim shift gives the pair a pleasing give.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-halant: Blockletter paints at constant width, like a sign-painter's single brush stroke, and Halant, a text serif, follows with towering lowercase. And its faint, real thick-thin shift keeps the body from simply copying the heading.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-hedvig-letters: Hedvig Letters Serif reads with open-ended curves and a tall, sturdy lowercase, plus medium-key contrast in its forms. Blockletter looks bent from one wire, so it frames that body crisply.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-marcellus-sc: Pencil-sketched and tall in the belly, Blockletter keeps horizontals as thick as verticals. Marcellus SC, a text serif, would read with a lightly swelling rhythm and pulled-back terminals, dignified and literary over many lines.
